items.prompt:
A flaw in reasoning is called a:
A) fallacy
B) claim
C) title

Presenting only two choices when more exist is a:
A) false dilemma
B) valid argument
C) definition

Drawing a broad conclusion from too few cases is a:
A) hasty generalization
B) sound argument
C) definition

'If we let students use phones, next they'll stop learning and society will collapse.' This is a:
A) slippery-slope fallacy
B) sound argument
C) valid proof

'You're either with us or against us' is a:
A) false dilemma
B) strong argument
C) definition

steps: Only two options. Key is A.

items.prompt:
A strong argument has:
A) valid reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence
B) a personal attack
C) a single rare example
items.answer: A) valid reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence

steps: Valid + relevant + sufficient. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) valid reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence

items.prompt:
Read.

'Don't trust his economic plan; he failed his driving test twice.'

This is a(n):
A) ad hominem fallacy
B) valid rebuttal
C) relevant evidence

steps: Attacks him, not the plan. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which argument is STRONGEST?
A) 'The program works: a controlled study of 1,000 students showed a 20% gain.'
B) 'The program works because the principal likes it.'
C) 'The program works; everyone says so.'
items.answer: A) 'The program works: a controlled study of 1,000 students showed a 20% gain.'

steps: Relevant, sufficient data. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'The program works: a controlled study of 1,000 students showed a 20% gain.'
